findings.claim: The spec names three environmental challenges: deforestation, increased carbon dioxide levels leading to potential global warming, and the need for fair trade.
findings.truth: The specification treats these as environmental, social and economic challenges; fair trade is not solely an environmental challenge.

findings.claim: Fair trade ensures that producers in developing countries receive fair payment and work in safe conditions.
findings.truth: Fairtrade standards seek fairer prices and safer working conditions, but Fairtrade says its standards alone cannot ensure that every worker has fair wages and decent conditions.
findings.evidence: Fairtrade, What is Fairtrade? and Objectives of the standards

findings.claim: Forests managed so that trees are replanted at the same rate they are harvested.
findings.truth: Sustainable forest management can use natural or artificial regeneration after harvesting; it is not defined by replanting at an identical rate.

findings.claim: “nothing should be in your houses that you do not know to be useful or believe to be beautiful”
findings.truth: The verified wording is “Have nothing in your houses that you do not know to be useful, or believe to be beautiful.”
findings.evidence: National Portrait Gallery, The Beauty of Life (1880), fetched 2026-09-06

findings.claim: You must study at least one category in depth for your NEA.
findings.truth: Students must develop and apply in-depth knowledge in relation to at least one material category or system; the requirement is not limited to the NEA.

findings.claim: Injection moulding requires an expensive steel mould ... For 500 units, injection moulding is more cost-effective overall.
findings.truth: Injection moulding can use aluminium or steel tooling. The economical choice at 500 units depends on the part, tooling and supplier costs, so it cannot be fixed from quantity alone.
findings.evidence: Protolabs, Aluminum vs. Steel Tooling and Making (Light) Waves

findings.claim: Computer Numerical Control — a subtractive process where a computer-controlled tool cuts material from a solid block.
findings.truth: CNC is the automatic control of a process using numerical data; routing and milling are examples of subtractive CNC operations.

findings.claim: Timber — general tolerance of ±2 mm for hand-cut joints.
findings.truth: The specification gives ±2 mm as an example, not as a general timber-joint tolerance. Retain it only if it is a stated local workshop rule; otherwise describe the tolerance as depending on the required fit and process, then align the related knowledge check.
findings.ruling: NOTE: ±2 mm is the spec's own worked example for hand-cut timber joints; a usable classroom rule of thumb, left.

summary: Seven lessons were checked. Seven verified factual corrections are supplied, and one context-dependent tolerance claim is left for adjudication.
